claims.claim: Origen of Alexandria was an early Christian theologian and ascetic who lived from approximately 185 to 253 CE.
Origen was born in Alexandria, Egypt, and was educated in the Catechetical School of Alexandria under Pantaenus and Clement of Alexandria.
Origen became head of the Catechetical School of Alexandria, first informally and then officially in 203 CE.
Origen wrote homilies on the book of Ruth, among many other biblical books.
The total body of Origen's work has not been preserved.
Origen's homilies treated Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Joshua, Judges, Ruth, 1 Samuel, Song of Songs, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, and Luke.
A Greek text of Origen's work 'In Ruth' survives, which includes commentary on Ruth as a type of the Gentiles who left her ancestral customs and was united with Israel.
Origen was one of the most influential and controversial figures in early Christian theology, and was later considered a heretic by some.
Origen made copious use of the allegorical method in his commentaries.
Origen was described by John Anthony McGuckin as 'the greatest genius the early church ever produced'.
